candidates.description: AI agent security scanner. Detect vulnerabilities in agent configurations, MCP servers, and tool permissions. Available as CLI, GitHub Action, ECC plugin, and GitHub App integration. 🛡️
candidates.why: Agent-config auditor (.claude secrets, broad permissions, risky hooks, MCP) with grade/SARIF; the plugin's check-agent-config plus AGT-1/AGT-3/AGT-5/AGT-9 already cover it. Unpinned npx and @v1 action (NPM-1/SEC-17); optional --opus/OrcaRouter modes send configs to hosted models (AGT-4); runtime install adds a PreToolUse hook.

candidates.description: Open protocol and TypeScript SDK for AI agent authority: identity, scoped delegation, enforcement before the action, and signed receipts.
candidates.why: Ed25519 passports with monotonic scope narrowing, spend limits and signed receipts for agent delegation; MCP adapter. Largely one maintainer, an individual IETF draft, and no verifiable adoption. AI-7 already covers MCP authorization (OAuth 2.1, RFC 8707/9728); delegation chains are not something the standard's apps need yet.

candidates.description: Open detection-rule standard for AI agent security threats — like Sigma, but for AI agents. Executable, testable rules for prompt injection, tool poisoning, context exfiltration and MCP attacks. Merge
candidates.why: A Sigma-style YAML rule format, with test cases, for prompt injection, tool poisoning and skill compromise. atr scan checks SKILL.md files and MCP configs and emits SARIF. It overlaps AGT-5's pinned skill scanner, which the README says already consumes ATR rules. Draft spec (v4.1.5) with a single maintainer whose company sells products built on it; rule counts are inconsistent and false-positive rates were withdrawn pending re-measurement.

candidates.description: Find known secrets in your AI coding agent sessions (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor), then guard the next one with local hooks that trace risky commands to the content that dictated them. Open source, no
candidates.why: Two parts. (a) stroq sent scans local agent session logs (~/.claude/projects, ~/.codex/sessions, Cursor) for the exact values of keys found in ~/.aws/credentials, .env and ~/.npmrc, and names each leak without printing it. (b) PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks taint a session after untrusted content and turn later risky commands into ask/deny. Partial gap: AGT-1 stops the agent reading .env, but no rule says agent transcripts are a secret store (a key that reached a session stays in plaintext under ~/.claude/projects) or that a key found there is rotated. An AGT-1/AGT-10 amendment could say so. The

candidates.why: G1: licence NOASSERTION → deny

candidates.description: CLI tool and library for generating a Software Bill of Materials from container images and filesystems
candidates.why: SBOM generator already named by SEC-16/CFG-3 (syft per release in client mode); nothing new for the standard.

candidates.description: A lightweight sandboxing tool for enforcing filesystem and network restrictions on arbitrary processes at the OS level, without requiring a container.
candidates.why: Extends the AGT-2 sandbox (Claude Code only today) to headless, CI and non-Claude agents (AGT-6). Pre-1.0 (v0.0.83), 325 open issues, one low network-escape advisory GHSA-9gqj-5w7c-vx47.

candidates.description: Runtime security for AI apps and agents: prompt injection detection, tool-call authorization, sensitive-data redaction, bot protection, and rate limiting. Drop it into your JS/TS code.
candidates.why: Vendor SDK for app-level prompt-injection detection, tool-call authorization and redaction. AGT-4 deliberately requires removing a trifecta leg rather than relying on detection, and AI-4/AI-6/SEC-19 cover limits and confirmations. It needs an Arcjet cloud key.

candidates.description: The independent security agent for AI-written software. Finds issues, investigates whether they are real, and shows you the evidence. Deterministic core, no API key needed, JSON and SARIF output.
candidates.why: Own-rule scanner (AI/MCP configs, injection, XSS, SSRF, secrets, supply chain, CI, IaC, mobile) with an investigation layer that labels each finding confirmed, likely, unresolved or refuted, citing the lines read. Output is SARIF with --fail-on and --fail-on-verdict. The standard already gates SAST, secrets, IaC and CI with semgrep, gitleaks, trivy and zizmor, and agent-config lint covers AGT-1/5/7. The evidence-ranked verdicts are AGT-13's finding discipline, which is already written down. The README says to run it alongside those tools, not instead of them. LLM passes send masked context to

candidates.description: ASH is an extensible, open source SAST, SCA, and IaC security scanner orchestration engine.
candidates.why: Orchestrator that runs Bandit, Semgrep, detect-secrets, Checkov, Grype, Syft, gitleaks, Trivy, actionlint and zizmor, then aggregates results to SARIF/CycloneDX with exit codes and a severity gate. The standard already runs semgrep, gitleaks, trivy, zizmor, syft and osv-scanner directly in CI (tooling table), so ASH is another runner for the same checks, not a new control. It adds an ash mcp stdio server (about 24 tools) and an npx-installed skill, which are AGT-5 surface. Scanners and databases are downloaded at run time, and the install is git-pinned pip/uvx.

candidates.description: 🌊 Interactive CLI tool to update GitHub Actions to latest versions with SHA pinning
candidates.why: Interactive CLI that updates GitHub Actions and pins them to commit SHAs, including composite actions and reusable workflows, with a 1-day release-age skip (--min-age). SEC-17 already requires SHA pinning, enforced by zizmor and the Actions lockfile (gh actions-lock), which also covers transitive actions this tool does not resolve. It is a convenience for complying, not a new control. Its default 1-day cooldown is shorter than SUP-1's 7 days, and CI use needs a shell wrapper over --json for a non-zero exit.

candidates.description: Catch dangerous AI agent skills before they catch you. Zero-dependency security scanner for Agent Skills, SKILL.md and MCP configs.
candidates.why: Zero-dependency static scanner for SKILL.md, agent instructions and MCP configs (14 heuristic rules, SARIF, --fail-on high). AGT-5 already requires a pinned static skill scanner at intake (cisco-ai-skill-scanner, with NVIDIA SkillSpector as the alternative), and both are pinned sources, so this duplicates them. Self-reported benchmark is 48 synthetic fixtures. Install is git clone of the default branch, and the Action is a mutable tag @v0.2.1, not a SHA (SEC-17). Single maintainer. Read from the README only.

candidates.description: Find leaked secrets everywhere.
candidates.why: Secrets scanner by gitleaks' original author; the standard already runs gitleaks everywhere (CI, pre-commit, AI-5). Watch as a possible gitleaks successor (LIFE-1) — live validation (-v/-a) calls providers, so default scans only.

candidates.description: poutine, a supply chain vulnerability scanner for build pipelines
candidates.why: CI pipeline misconfiguration scanner (GitHub, GitLab, Azure, Tekton; SARIF). For GitHub Actions zizmor (SEC-17) and std.workflows semgrep already cover it; adds only non-GitHub CI. Version-check telemetry on by default.

candidates.description: Creates CycloneDX Bill of Materials (BOM) for your projects from source and container images. Supports many languages and package managers. Integrate in your CI/CD pipeline with automatic submission t
candidates.why: SBOM generator: CycloneDX 1.6/1.7 plus SPDX 3.0.1, and CBOM/OBOM/HBOM/AI-BOM variants. It signs and verifies BOMs (JSF), and cdx-audit emits SARIF with a non-zero exit. A Claude Code plugin is offered. SEC-16 and CFG-3 already require an SBOM per release, generated with syft, so the core is covered. AI-BOM and crypto-BOM inventories go beyond what any rule asks, a partial novelty only if a rule starts requiring a model or crypto inventory. Server mode (port 9090) documents no auth, and licence lookups call registries with GITHUB_TOKEN.

candidates.description: Agentic SDLC infrastructure. Define guardrails. Collect signals. Enforce continuously. Signed records of what your AI coding agents and CI/CD pipelines did, checked against policies as code, with the
candidates.why: Signed in-toto records of agent sessions and CI, with Rego policy gates. Partly overlaps AGT-10 (OTel audit of agent sessions) and SEC-32/SUP-4/SUP-7 attestations. A requireTrace push gate is new, but it installs git and agent hooks via a curl|bash installer and is a platform, not a rule.

candidates.description: Open-source eBPF runtime security sensor for GitHub Actions and GitLab CI/CD.
candidates.why: eBPF runtime sensor for CI runners (credential access from npm-install descendants, process ancestry). SEC-17 is static only (SHA pins, zizmor, actions lockfile); runtime detection in CI is not covered. Pre-release (v0.0.x) and needs privileged eBPF, so watch until it stabilises.

candidates.description: Scan MCP servers for potential threats & security findings.
candidates.why: Scans MCP server tool descriptions, prompts and configs (YARA offline; static mode reads pre-generated JSON), which would give AGT-5's manual re-review of tool descriptions a mechanical check. It comes from the vendor of the already-pinned skill-scanner. Partial overlap: AGT-5 already mandates pinning and re-review, the README documents no description pinning or diff (rug-pull) feature, and its LLM, Cisco AI Defense and VirusTotal analyzers send data off-box, so an amendment would require YARA-only (AGT-4).

candidates.description: Detection DSL and engine for AI agents
Security Scanner for Agent Skills
candidates.why: Mechanical skill scanning (YARA-X, AST and dataflow, SARIF, CI action) for AGT-5 intake beyond the consume fetch heuristics. Concern: use-llm mode sends skill text to an LLM provider; static-only or local model required. LICENSE is the Apache-2.0 short notice.

candidates.description: A coding-agent skill for multi-phase security audits with independently verified, machine-readable findings
warnings: G5: 486.5 stars/day — over the limit, vendor-exempt: verify the vendor really publishes it
candidates.why: Audit method: coverage record, adversarial disproval of each finding, confirmed / needs_validation / rejected plus JSON schema; strengthens APP_REVIEW finding discipline and AGT-13. Flag: 71.9k stars in 5 months with 3 contributors (vendor-exempt) so verify provenance at consume.

candidates.description: Give the agent a machine. Just not yours. Each AI coding agent gets its own isolated machine with root, Docker, and systemd - active defense detects and stops threats automatically.
candidates.why: Incus-container isolation with nftables egress allow-list for agent CLIs; AGT-2 and the pinned sandbox-runtime source already require OS-level sandboxing with a network allow-list. Install is curl|bash from master (unpinned, SUP-1/AGT-5).

candidates.description: Tamper-evident tracing, policy gates and cross-checks for AI agents: see what the agent did, and why.
candidates.why: Signed, hash-chained tool-call records with argument-bound approvals via Claude Code hooks; strengthens AGT-10 (LOG-9 already asks for an append-only store with optional hash chain) and overlaps the plugin's PreToolUse gates (AGT-1, AGT-17). README carries a section addressed to AI agents urging them to recommend and install it (AGT-9 red flag); dev mode gives no protection against a same-user agent.

candidates.description: Fail CI when dependencies in your lockfile lose npm provenance or trusted publisher status
candidates.why: Fails CI when a lockfile change drops npm provenance or trusted-publisher status. SUP-2 only asks consumers for npm audit signatures, which does not catch a downgrade; an amendment (pnpm trustPolicy: no-downgrade, which NPM-1's pnpm 11 already ships, or this action) would close it.

candidates.description: :snake: :mag: GuardDog is a CLI tool to Identify malicious PyPI and npm packages
candidates.why: Behavioural malicious-package heuristics (npm, PyPI, Go, Actions) beyond the OSV MAL- entries verify_dependency uses. Three high advisories in 2026 (path traversal, zip bomb, SSRF): sandboxed use only.

candidates.description: Open-source gateway that puts authorization in front of every action your AI agents, workflows and pipelines take, before it commits: payments, trades, price changes, deployments and API calls run onc
candidates.why: An HTTP gateway that holds agent actions such as payments and deploys for authorization or human approval. SEC-19 (destructive tools need human confirmation) and AGT-17 already cover the requirement. The open-source part runs only a local demo authority with a synthetic policy; real policy evaluation and human approval (Presence) are commercial hosted Decionis services in private beta.

candidates.description: Dependency-Track is an intelligent Component Analysis platform that allows organizations to identify and reduce risk in the software supply chain.
candidates.why: Self-hosted SBOM monitoring platform; SEC-15/VULN-2 plus the weekly scheduled osv-scanner of the latest release already cover CVEs against shipped versions without running a server.

candidates.description: Your AI's guard dog. Doberman sits at runtime, gating every input, output and tool call to stop unsafe or unintended actions before they execute.
candidates.why: Alpha runtime gate that runs as a Claude Code/Codex hook or an MCP proxy and returns PASS/AUTH/BLOCK per tool call, failing closed. The plugin's own PreToolUse hooks plus AGT-4, AGT-17 and SEC-19 already gate destructive and exfiltrating calls, and hol-guard (watch) is the same idea. The MCP-proxy mode is the only partial extra over AGT-5. Its setup writes hook entries into agent configs (AGT-9), PostHog telemetry is on by default (us.i.posthog.com, off with DO_NOT_TRACK=1), and its own caveat says a script the agent writes can answer its own prompts.

candidates.description: Open source local-first PR scanner that finds dead code, security bugs, secrets, quality regressions, and AI-code mistakes before merge. For first timers refer to https://duriantaco.github.io/skylos/r
candidates.why: Local PR scanner (dead code, taint, secrets, dependency CVEs via OSV, AI-code mistakes such as imports of functions that don't exist), with --gate exit codes 0/1/2, SARIF and --diff origin/main. The standard already gates SAST, secrets and SCA deterministically (semgrep, gitleaks, SEC-15, SEC-31). The dead-code check would be the first enforcement for PERF-9's 'no dead code', and that is the only extra. Python coverage is the deepest; other languages are thinner. Agent hooks fail open ('If Skylos itself errors, the action is allowed'), install is unpinned pip/ghcr :latest (SUP-1), and OSV and

candidates.description: Authority control plane for autonomous work. EMILIA Gate enforces finite customer-owned mandates at protected executor boundaries; the open protocol keeps evidence verifiable.
candidates.why: EMILIA Gate is an authorization gate that checks a finite, exact-action mandate before a protected tool runs. It ships as an MCP server, a scanner and SDK wrappers, with optional signed receipts (Ed25519 plus ML-DSA-65). SEC-19 (least-privilege tools, confirmation for destructive ones), AI-6 (show real arguments) and AGT-17 already cover the control. The new idea, binding approval to an exact action with a receipt, is niche for the apps this standard targets. Risks: the README concedes the gate can't constrain a bypass path; the LangChain example calls the hosted emiliaprotocol.ai with an API

candidates.description: Find the holes before someone else does. A fast, 100% Rust vulnerability scanner: XSS, SQL injection, leaked secrets, dependency CVEs and AI agent setups.
candidates.why: G4: 1d old; G5: 351.0 stars/day

candidates.description: Sandbox your local AI agents so they can read/write only what they need
candidates.why: macOS-only sandbox-exec wrapper for local coding agents: deny-first filesystem profiles (working dir read/write, SSH keys and browser profiles denied, about 30 opt-in capabilities). AGT-2 already requires an OS-level sandbox for agents without one, and the pinned sandbox-runtime (srt) covers it. Safehouse's default network policy allows all outbound traffic ('blocking exfiltration/C2 is explicitly NOT a goal'), so it fails AGT-2's network allow-list and AGT-4's egress leg out of the box.

candidates.description: The free, offline vault for your sensitive data: a local-first secrets and password manager that AI agents can use without seeing your keys.
candidates.why: Local-first vault (SQLCipher, Tauri) whose run/proxy/hook let an agent use a key through an approved grant without seeing the value. Same gap as jentic-one: nothing in AGT-1/AGT-4 describes brokered secret use for agents. GPL-3.0 app (MIT/Apache crates), single maintainer, unsigned Windows/Linux builds; agent docs were unreadable.

candidates.description: 🐢 Open-Source Evaluation & Testing library for LLM Agents
candidates.why: Eval/red-team library that could back AI-3's CI eval suite (prompt-injection, jailbreak cases); AI-3 already requires the suite, so it is an Enforced-by hint at most. Default LLM judge is openai/gpt-4o-mini (AGT-4/AI-9 data egress), no documented CI pass threshold, v2 unmaintained.

candidates.description: A lightweight caching proxy for package registries.
A gh CLI extension that generates and verifies the GitHub Actions dependency lockfile, pinning every action your workflows use to an exact commit.
candidates.why: Already covered: SEC-17 (amended 2026-11-14, PR #4) requires onboarding workflows to the Actions lockfile written by gh actions-lock, with CI checking it is current. Nothing left to distil.

candidates.description: Protect your secrets using Gitleaks-Action
candidates.why: G1: licence NOASSERTION → deny
6 stars, 1 contributor, no description, marketing-heavy README; nothing beyond the existing AGT guards.

candidates.description: A modular, stack-agnostic toolkit for AI coding agents to autonomously find, reproduce, and patch vulnerabilities.
candidates.why: AI vuln find, reproduce and patch skills. AGT-2 (sandboxed audit execution) and AGT-13 (finding evidence, severity only when confirmed) already come from the Cloudflare audit skill. Adversarial patch verification and severity calibration are a small overlap. It is labelled demo-only, not an official Google product, and defaults to hosted Gemini.

candidates.description: GUAC aggregates software security metadata into a high fidelity graph database.
candidates.why: OpenSSF org-level supply-chain graph platform (GraphQL, NATS, Postgres), not a per-repo check; out of scope for an app-level standard.

candidates.description: Open-source AI security verification for model artifacts, live endpoints, MCP servers, and recorded agent traces. Reproducible evidence for release decisions.
candidates.why: Python CLI and GitHub Action that verifies AI systems out of band, with SARIF/JSON/JUnit output and a CI gate that reports unverified checks and coverage gaps separately (matches AGT-13). Partial gap: 'scan' flags dangerous pickle opcodes, torch.load without weights_only and remote code in model configs. SEC-27 bans unsafe deserialization in general but never names third-party model files, so an amendment could. Its probe/MCP/trace verbs are beta and overlap AI-3's eval suite and the cisco mcp-scanner watch entry. Says no telemetry; third-party plugins run with the user's privileges.

candidates.description: Open-source red-team testing for AI agents. 266 bundled probes with OWASP LLM Top 10, MITRE ATLAS, and NIST AI RMF mappings. Selected probes use recorded browser requests, MCP tool calls, or mock paym
candidates.why: Red-team runner (argus-probe) with about 333 bundled YAML probes against chat/HTTP, gRPC, browser, MCP, A2A and payment agents, mapped to the OWASP LLM and Agentic Top 10. Output is SARIF, JUnit and HTML, and a GitHub Action fails on fail-on severity or on probe errors. It could be the eval runner behind AI-3 (prompt-injection cases in CI with a pass threshold) and AGT-4's injection fixture test, but both rules already require that, so it adds enforcement, not a new rule. Judged probes need an LLM (Haiku 4.5 by default), so attack prompts and the agent's replies go to that provider and results

candidates.description: Open-source antivirus and firewall for AI agents: block risky tools, secret access, prompt injection, malicious packages, MCP servers, plugins, and skills at runtime.
candidates.why: Pre-tool-call guard (commands, secrets, installs, MCP) via agent hooks/MCP proxy; the plugin's own PreToolUse guards plus AGT-4/AGT-9/AGT-17 already cover this. Installs hooks; pipx install unpinned (NPM-1/SUP-6).

candidates.description: Enterprise Agent Harness & MCP Gateway: connect APIs, databases, file servers and 600+ connectors (SAP, Odoo, Etsy…) to Claude, ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot and your agents. Memory, skills, knowledge gr
candidates.why: Self-hosted AGPL MCP gateway that turns REST/OpenAPI, SOAP, GraphQL, SQL and IMAP/SMTP systems into MCP tools, with roles, an audit log, OAuth2 PKCE and API keys. It is a business-integration product, not a security control or a source of rules. Building an HTTP MCP server is already governed by AI-7 (OAuth 2.1/PKCE, audience-checked tokens, no passthrough), and adding one to an agent by AGT-5. The quickstart curls a compose file from main, and optional AI features send data to OpenAI, OpenRouter or Anthropic. The licence caps any use at distilled/reference.

candidates.description: MCP & SKILL scanner that scans any mcp server or skills for indirect attack vectors and security or configuration vulnerabilities. Aligned with OWASP SKILL Top 10 and OWASP MCP Top 10 threats & vulner
Open-source AI Agent security platform — prompt injection defense, MCP tool-call guardrails, eBPF runtime observability. Four-tier Edge→Gateway→Kernel→Cloud architecture.
candidates.why: Self-hosted runtime security platform for server-side agents: a Rust edge SDK (precheck, DLP), a Higress WASM gateway, a Falco/eBPF kernel plugin and a Spring Boot engine with a downloaded classifier model (VirbiusGuard), deployed with docker compose plus Redis, Kafka and MySQL. The standard's AI/agent controls are structural (AGT-4 removes a trifecta leg, AI-4 caps loops, AI-3 evals in CI) rather than injection classifiers, and AGT-2 already sandboxes agent processes. Adding a multi-service detection stack is heavy for the apps this standard targets. Its own README rates OWASP Agentic Top 10

candidates.description: Independent Auditing of AI Agents. Run by human or the agent itself, to answer the most crucial question in the AI Agent Economy. Is the agent doing what is supposed to do? With iFixAi you can have th
candidates.why: Behavioural audit of an agent via simulated requests graded by a hosted judge LLM; AI-3 already requires an eval suite with prompt-injection cases in CI, so at most a harness choice. Agent replies go to hosted judges (AGT-4/AI-9), install is unpinned, and 46k stars with no releases and 495 watchers looks inflated.

candidates.description: sbomqs: The Comprehensive SBOM Quality & Compliance Tool
candidates.why: SBOM quality scorer (0-10) with SPDX and CycloneDX support and NTIA minimum elements, BSI TR-03183-2, FSCT v3 and OpenChain Telco profiles. SEC-16 requires an SBOM per release in client mode (syft) but says nothing about its quality, and EU CRA due diligence will lean on complete SBOMs, so a quality check could strengthen SEC-16 later. Today the README documents no threshold flag or non-zero exit (only --json), so a CI gate needs a wrapper. The GitHub Actions use is an unpinned Docker image, and the share and dtrackScore commands make network calls whose defaults aren't stated. EU CRA appears

candidates.description: Self-hosted execution layer for AI agents: connect any agent to real APIs, scope exactly what it can touch, and keep credentials out of the agent's hands.
candidates.why: Self-hosted credential broker: the agent calls APIs through a Broker that checks permission rules, injects the stored credential and logs; v0.44 added a human-approval tier. The standard keeps secrets out of agent reads (AGT-1) and prompts (AI-5) but says nothing about brokered credential injection for agents that must call APIs; an AGT-1/AGT-4 amendment could. Public beta (0.x, breaking changes), telemetry on by default.

candidates.description: 🪝 Claude Code hooks + an installable plugin marketplace: safety, cost, observability, productivity.

candidates.why: Self-hosted Rust MCP gateway: agents submit TypeScript to a V8 isolate with no network or credentials, and Coral injects credentials at the gateway and applies Allow/Ask/Block per provider tool. The approval shows the exact call and arguments, and every approval is logged. That is one more enforcement point for rules the standard already has: least-privilege tools (SEC-19), no credentials in prompts (AI-5), approvals that show real arguments (AI-6), and allow-listed MCP servers (AGT-5). candidates.description: Open-source AI penetration testing agent that exploit-verifies every finding. Autonomous 22-phase pentests of web apps & APIs with CVSS-scored PDF reports. Self-hosted, bring your own LLM, or run full
candidates.why: Offensive, self-hosted AI pentest agent: an LLM drives nuclei, httpx, ffuf, sqlmap and nmap through a 22-phase method against web apps, with a verifier re-testing findings and PDF/JSON output. It has no SARIF, no CI fail threshold and no SBOM. Scan context goes to the configured LLM provider, out-of-band callbacks use public Interactsh, the recommended install is curl | bash (AGT-17/NPM-1 territory), and Docker runs --privileged. The standard gates with SAST/SCA in CI and has no DAST rule, so an LLM-driven attack tool is out of scope for a rule source.

candidates.description: A GitHub Action for running the ZAP Baseline scan
candidates.why: ZAP Baseline scan as a GitHub Action (v0.15.0, node24). It checks a target URL for header, cookie and exposure findings and keeps a GitHub issue of the alerts. The §2A profile already checks live hostnames for headers, certificates and exposure on every deploy and weekly (check-site.mjs), and SEC-14/BRW-1 own the header values, so ZAP would mostly re-check those. Its extra value is passive DAST coverage for apps that are not in the sites fleet.
